revenue_scope: Worldwide: Teva's single combined Treanda and Bendeka line in the specialty medicines segment revenue breakdown by therapeutic area and key products
why_separate: From the first quarter of 2016 Teva prints one line for Treanda and Bendeka together (Bendeka launched in the United States in January 2016); Treanda alone is not printed again, so the line is broader than the product and is not spliced onto the Treanda series, which ends 2015Q4.
notes: Covers 2016Q1-2017Q4, the quarters in which Teva still printed this combined line on a worldwide, product-type basis (the specialty medicines segment). From 2018Q1 Teva prints the line only inside geographic segment tables (see teva_treanda_cont_na, 2018Q1-2023Q4, and teva_treanda_cont_us, 2024Q1-2026Q2, which have different territories). Labels as printed: 'Treanda and Bendeka' through 2017Q3, 'Bendeka and Treanda' for 2017Q4 (the Q4 2017 release). Teva's text compares the combined 2016 quarters with the prior-year quarter 'Treanda only'. Annual checks: 155+207+149+150=661, equal to the 661 printed for 2016 in the Q4 2016 release and the 2016 20-F; 157+163+181+157=658, equal to the 658 printed for 2017 in the Q4 2017 release. The Q1 2017 comparative column in the Q1 2018 release (156, North America segment) differs by 1 from the 157 printed here (the two are different territories).
search_log: Listed every Teva filing from data.sec.gov submissions (CIK 818686, recent file and the 1996-2017 history file) filed 2016-04-01 to 2026-09-01. Fetched every htm document of every 10-Q, 10-K, 10-K/A, 20-F, 20-F/A, 8-K/A, 6-K and 6-K/A, and of every 8-K that carries item 2.02 (929 documents). 8-Ks without item 2.02 were not opened, so an absence below holds only for the documents read. Exhibits 3x/21/23/10 and XBRL R files were skipped.

Extracted every table row whose first cell names the product (and, for Treanda, BENDEKA) from those documents and read the heading above each table for the segment it belongs to; each quarter was taken from that quarter's own earnings release (8-K Exhibit 99.1, or the 6-K body/exhibit in 2016-2017), where the quarter is the current-period column.
Partners and royalty holders (for the bendamustine products, Eagle Pharmaceuticals) were not searched: that licence is for royalties on Bendeka and no Eagle document was read.

Q1 2016 6-K (the first document printing the combined line): the row reads 'Treanda and Bendeka 155 157' and the text says 'Treanda and Bendeka combined sales in the first quarter of 2016 amounted to $155 million, compared to $157 million in the first quarter of 2015 (Treanda only)'.

Checked the 2016 20-F: its annual table reads 'Treanda 661 741 767' for 2016, 2015, 2014 and its text says 'Treanda and Bendeka combined revenues were $661 million in 2016'; the label is Treanda but the 2016 figure is the combined one, so no separate Treanda-only figure exists for any 2016 period in the documents read.

continuation.evidence: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/818686/000119312516583103/d172918d6k.htm: "Treanda and Bendeka combined sales in the first quarter of 2016 amounted to $155 million, compared to $157 million in the first quarter of 2015 (Treanda only)"; "Bendeka, which was launched in the United States in January 2016, is a liquid, low-volume (50 mL) and short-time 10-minute infusion formulation of bendamustine hydrochloride that we licensed from Eagle to complement our Treanda franchise."
